# Decision log

Format: **D-n · date · decision** — context / alternatives / consequences.

---

### D-1 · 2026-11-02 · Static site generated by GitHub Actions, deployed with `actions/deploy-pages`
Generated HTML is uploaded as a Pages artifact, not committed to the repo.
*Alternatives:* commit `site/` to a `gh-pages` branch (noisy history, a commit every night).
*Consequence:* Pages source must be set to "GitHub Actions" once.

### D-2 · 2026-11-02 · Python 3.12, stdlib HTTP + PyYAML, icalendar, recurring-ical-events
Small dependency set, no web framework, no Jinja (HTML built with f-strings + `html.escape`).
*Alternatives:* Node/Eleventy, Jinja2. Python chosen for readable scrapers and simple tests.

### D-3 · 2026-11-02 · City of Helsinki Linked Events API is the primary source
It aggregates City of Helsinki culture, library, youth and many partner events and
powers tapahtumat.hel.fi / MyHelsinki. Open, no API key.
*Note:* api.hel.fi was not reachable from the development sandbox, so the
integration is built against the documented schema and tested with fixtures
only — must be verified on the first real GitHub Actions run (see backlog B-1).

### D-4 · 2026-11-02 · Scope is limited by configuration (user choice)
Linked Events has thousands of events per month. Server-side filter: `division=helsinki`
+ a list of YSO culture keywords (OR). Client-side: title regex excludes for
recurring library/children activities; `event_type` defaults to General, so courses
are excluded by the API. Recurring/umbrella parent events are dropped (`super_event_type=none`).
*Alternatives considered:* show everything; curated-only.

### D-5 · 2026-11-02 · Summaries come from the source text, trimmed (~220 chars) (user choice)
HTML is stripped and text is cut at a sentence boundary when possible.
*Alternative:* Claude API summaries during the build (needs API key + cost) — kept in backlog.

### D-6 · 2026-11-02 · Finnish UI; event texts in Finnish with English → Swedish fallback (user choice)

### D-7 · 2026-11-02 · Generic source types: `manual`, `linkedevents`, `ical`, `jsonld`
"Web pages" are supported first via schema.org Event JSON-LD, which many venue and
ticket sites embed, so most pages need only a URL. Site-specific HTML scrapers are
added only when needed (plug-in module per source).

### D-8 · 2026-11-02 · Schedule uses GitHub's cron `timezone: Europe/Helsinki`
`cron: "0 3 * * *"` with `timezone` (supported since March 2026) gives 03:00 local time
in both summer and winter time.
*Alternative:* two UTC crons + DST gate script. GitHub scheduled runs can be delayed
a few minutes at busy times; acceptable.

### D-9 · 2026-11-02 · Fault tolerance
A failing source is logged and marked in the footer; others still publish. If the total
event count is zero the build fails, so the previous page stays online. The page also
self-corrects "today" in the browser if it is opened on a later day than it was built.

### D-10 · 2026-11-02 · Long events go to a separate collapsed section
Events longer than `max_event_days` (7) — mainly exhibitions — would otherwise appear
in "today" every day. They are listed under "Pitkäkestoiset".

### D-11 · 2026-11-02 · De-duplication by normalised title + start minute + place
First source in config order wins; missing fields are filled from duplicates. Manual
source is listed first so hand-made corrections override API data.

### D-12 · 2026-11-02 · Adding events: YAML files in `events/manual/`, fed by Claude and GitHub issues
Issue form (`add-event.yml`) → workflow converts to YAML, commits, closes the issue and
triggers the build. Issues by OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR are processed immediately;
others need the `hyväksytty` label (spam protection). The issue body is passed to the
script via an environment variable (no shell interpolation → no script injection).
`CLAUDE.md` documents the same format for Claude.

### D-13 · 2026-11-02 · Code delivered via the user's local clone
The development session had no push rights to the repository; files were written to
the local clone (`~/Code/helsinkievents`) and the user commits/pushes.

### D-14 · 2026-11-02 · Include-keyword file `config/keywords.yaml` decides what is shown
User asked for music, performances and openings only. Categories with plain word stems
(substring, case-insensitive; `re:` for regex) are matched against title + source tags
(summary too for openings, where the word is often only in the description), plus an
exclude list. Applied to all sources after fetching, so iCal/JSON-LD sources follow the
same rules. Manual events bypass the filter (they were added on purpose). Categories also
drive badges and filter buttons on the page.
*Alternatives:* only Linked Events server-side YSO keywords (too coarse, misses
openings, source-specific); Claude-based classification (cost, non-deterministic).
*Consequence:* the Linked Events YSO keyword list is now only a pre-filter to keep API
volume down; film (yso:p1235) was removed from it.
